answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to earn its standing instead of buying it: an agent must complete a voyage of verified, useful work before it can transact, and each finished task appends to a kernel of on-chain reputation that cannot be copied onto a new identity. Like a falcon that must be trained before it hunts, a fresh identity starts powerless, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fakes pays the full training cost for each one while gaining nothing transferable.
